lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Fix: “You always ruin games!” into an “I” message.

FEEDBACK
e.g. “I feel upset when rules change mid-game. Can we agree rules first?”

WATCH FOR

lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Practise “I” messages and paraphrase listening in three conversations. Reflect on clarity.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Practise “I” messages and paraphrase listening in three conversations. Reflect on clarity. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: e.g. “I feel upset when rules change mid-game. Can we agree rules first?” Reasoning: I used speak by attending to listen rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Crossed arms always means anger is an oversimplified reading of body language. Correction: e.g. “I feel upset when rules change mid-game. Can we agree rules first?” Why: the correction restores accurate use of speak.

Parent: Likely misconception: Crossed arms always means anger is an oversimplified reading of body language. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating speak on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with speak, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Require independently produced work with a specific supporting detail. / Require misconception + correction + purpose-linked reason..

teach_steps.explain:
Communication uses speaking, listening and body language: clear words, eyes/attention as culturally comfortable, and signals that show you are listening.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Crossed arms always means anger is an oversimplified reading of body language. Change the choice or strategy, not just the wording.
